# Phone showcase — Style Prompt

> One phone, centred in a calm pastel void, filmed by a virtual camera that never cuts: it pushes into the screen to read it, pulls back to let a card float out of it, and finally recedes so a single line of type can close the film. The phone is the window; the camera is the viewer's eye.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

The whole film is **one continuous take around one phone**. The phone sits on a soft, empty, slightly warm or lilac ground with ~50–60 % negative space. Proof is shown, not told: the screen scrolls, a card **lifts out of the screen** and floats in front of it, notifications **drop in above it**, a number **counts up** on a contrast card. Type is a short, bold, centred headline that **blurs in word by word** before the camera moves, and leaves before the camera dives. The film ends with **one hard cut to a dark end card**.

Native register: "it is this easy, and it is right here on your phone". That fits ordering, paying, booking and tracking from a shop, but just as well a creator's portfolio or channel, an app's feature, a course's lesson list, or a story told through the messages and photos on someone's screen.

Not a screen recording (the camera moves, cards leave the screen), not a slideshow of mock-ups (no cut between phone poses, one take), not a 3D-render showreel (flat vector UI, soft shadows, no chrome reflections), not a split-screen feature list (the phone stays centred; text lives above it, not beside it in columns).

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Ground**: a soft two-stop gradient (the brand's lightest tint → a slightly deeper tint) with two large soft colour blobs (the main colour at ~26 %, the accent at ~30 %) drifting slowly over the whole film. The blobs are radial gradients whose edge fades over ~240 px, not blurred shapes. No grain, no pattern, no grid.
- **Phone**: a near-black body with ~86 px radius on a ~580 px wide body, a hairline rim tinted with the main colour, a dynamic-island pill, and one long soft drop shadow (0 70px 120px, −40 spread). Width ≈ 52–55 % of a vertical frame at rest.
- **UI inside**: drawn with HTML/CSS: rounded cards (radius 26–36 px), pill chips and buttons, tiny soft shadows, the main colour on prices, active chips and buttons. Pictures are simple flat illustrations (shapes and gradients on a tinted tile), or the user's own photos cropped into the same rounded tile; never a screenshot pasted in a frame.
- **Floating UI**: cards outside the phone are a little larger than their in-screen twin (scale ~1.15–1.2), tilted 3–5°, with a deeper shadow. While a card floats, the phone behind it **defocuses** (blur ~5 px, opacity ~0.55) so depth reads without 3D.
- **The contrast card**: one card (stat, total, receipt) flips the text and surface colours; it is the only dark object on a light ground until the end card.
- **End card**: a fixed dark ground with a radial glow of the main colour behind the logo tile.

## 3. Colour logic

How the brand tokens fill the roles:

- `--latar` — the ground: the brand's lightest tint (cream, blush, lilac, mint). Never pure grey; never saturated. The gradient's far end, `--latar-ujung`, is `--latar` with 5 % of `--teks`, so it follows any brand.
- `--latar-2` — every floating card, list item and option pill. The phone's screen, `--layar`, sits between `--latar` and `--latar-2`; the search field and idle chips, `--isian`, are `--latar` with 3 % of `--teks`.
- `--teks` — headlines and all UI text; `--teks-redup` — labels and secondary lines.
- `--utama` — prices, the active chip, the action button, the selection ring, the payoff words of the headline, notification icons, chart bars, the end-card glow and logo tile. The only saturated colour on screen in most frames.
- `--teks-di-utama` — everything set on `--utama`: button labels, the badge count, the icon ticks, the logo's strokes.
- `--aksen` — one warm highlight (amber, butter yellow): a small tag ("Terlaris", "+38%") and one background blob. Text on it is `--teks-di-aksen`, the accent darkened toward black.
- The contrast card flips the pair: `--teks` as its ground, `--latar-2` as its text. On a light brand it is the one dark object; on a dark brand it becomes the one light object, and still reads.
- The look's own: `--gelap` with `--teks-gelap` (the end card: always near-black, tinted with 10 % of `--utama`, with white type), `--ponsel` (the device black), `--bayang` (the shadow tint), and `--kue-*` (illustration colours; their tiles are tints of them in `--latar-2`).

The headline puts `--utama` on the **second line** (the payoff words) and `--teks` on the first.

## 4. Type

- `--font-judul` carries headlines, product names, prices and numbers: a geometric or grotesk sans at its heaviest weight (Poppins 800 by default; Space Grotesk 700 is the more technical alternative).
- `--font-isi` carries labels, body lines and UI chrome: Poppins 500, with 800 only for small buttons, chips and tags.
- Headline: centred, 2 lines, ~100–120 px on 1080 wide, tracking −4 to −5 px, line height ~1.04, sentence case. Max ~4 words per line. A wider brand face needs a smaller size, never a third line.
- UI text inside the phone: 20–38 px at rest; it must become legible when the camera pushes in, not at rest.
- Numbers: tabular figures, count-ups of about 1.1 s, formatted in rupiah (Rp1.250.000; short form Rp110rb on notifications) or plain counts.
- Headline reveal: **blur 10 px → 0, rise 24 px, opacity 0 → 1, 0.5 s, `circ.out`, stagger ~0.09 s per word**. Exit: the reverse, 0.35 s `power1.in`, stagger 0.04 s.

## 5. Motion quality

- **One take.** References average ~4 cuts per minute; in a 15 s film that means **zero or one cut** (the cut to the end card). Everything else is camera.
- The camera is a wrapper around the whole world (phone + floating cards), scaled and translated with the transform origin at the phone's centre. Headlines live outside it, in screen space.
- **Camera moves are short and frequent**: median move ~0.37 s; push-ins ~0.5 s. Typical push-in factor **1.1–1.5×** (median ~1.18×); deep dives into the screen **1.5–2.1×**; pull-backs to **~0.8×** (median 0.83×) and a final recession to **~0.4–0.6×** (the example lands at 0.55×).
- **Eases (fitted from the references)**: arrivals and push-ins `circ.out` or `sine.out` (the two most common); dives into the screen `power2.inOut` / `power3.inOut`; scroll inside the phone `power2.inOut`, 1.1–1.5 s; departures `power1.in` / `power2.in`; slow drifts `sine.inOut` or linear.
- **Entrances**: phone rises from below the frame with a small 6–8° rotation settling to 0, ~1.1 s `circ.out`. Cards scale 0.7–0.9 → 1 in 0.45–0.7 s `circ.out`; lists and notifications stagger 0.06–0.16 s. Badges and small chips may overshoot (`back.out(1.7–3)`).
- **Taps** are a translucent touch dot with a rim that lands, presses (scale 0.8, 0.1 s yoyo), and a ripple from the button (scale 0 → 9, 0.5 s `circ.out`). Cursors are optional; touch dots are more native on a phone.
- **Rhythm**: hook headline by 0.8 s; the camera starts moving by 2.4 s; a new event every 1–1.5 s; final line of type held ≥ 1.5 s; end card held ≥ 2.4 s with a slow 1.06 → 1 settle.
- What never moves: the phone's horizontal centre. The camera may push off-centre to read a part of the screen, but every move resolves back to the axis.

## 6. Camera grammar

A vocabulary, not a route.

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Phone rises from below + slow push 1.0 → 1.12 (`circ.out`) | arrival, "here it is" | opening; a launch; a new menu; a new episode |
| Dive into the screen 1.5–2× (`power2.inOut`) | "look closely" | reading prices; a form; a booking slot; one message in a chat |
| Locked frame while the screen scrolls | abundance without cuts | a catalogue; a menu; a portfolio; a lesson list |
| Pull back to ~0.85–0.9× as a card lifts out | the chosen thing steps forward | a best-seller; the one package; a featured video; the key photo |
| Short punch 1.3× on a number (`circ.out`, ~0.5 s) | emphasis | a total; a discount; time saved; followers gained |
| Recession to ~0.4× (`power2.inOut`) | the phone becomes a detail of a bigger promise | the closing line; delivery options; a schedule; a guarantee |
| Hard cut to a dark end card | a full stop | logo, URL, call to action |

Transitions are camera moves or a defocus; no dissolves, no wipes, no slides between scenes.

## 7. Native moves

A menu: use the ones the story needs.

- **Blur-in headline over a waiting phone.** Two lines, word by word, then they evaporate upward as the camera moves. *Fits content like:* "Kue rumahan, sekali geser." for a home bakery; "Edit video cukup dari HP." for a creator's tutorial; "Belajar 10 menit sehari." for a language class; "Pesan terakhir darinya." opening a story told on a phone.
- **Dive and scroll.** The camera dives into the screen and holds while the list scrolls under it. *Fits content like:* a warung's daily menu; a creator's grid of past videos; a course's lessons; a chat scrolling back through a friendship.
- **The lift-out card.** One item rises out of the screen, bigger and tilted, the phone defocuses behind it, a tap confirms it and it flies into its icon. *Fits content like:* the best-selling brownies; the "cuci + setrika 3 kg" package; a creator's most-watched video saved to a playlist; the one photo the story turns on.
- **Notification rain.** Notifications drop in above the phone one after another, opaque cards with an icon in the main colour. *Fits content like:* incoming orders for a cake shop; bookings for a barbershop; comments on a creator's new post; students handing in homework; unanswered messages piling up in a story.
- **Contrast count-up card.** A contrast card slides up over the phone's lower half, a figure counts up and small bars grow. *Fits content like:* today's orders; subscribers this month; students enrolled; kilos washed this week; days without a reply.
- **Recede to the promise.** The phone shrinks to a small object and a bold two-line promise with pill chips takes the frame. *Fits content like:* "Pesan pagi, sampai sore." with Kirim kurir / Ambil di toko / Bayar QRIS; "Video baru tiap Jumat" for a channel; class times for a tutor; a story's last line.
- **Badge bump.** A count badge pops (`back.out(3)`) and the icon pulses once to confirm an action. *Fits content like:* cart count; a loyalty stamp; a new follower; a finished lesson; a message finally read.

## 8. Pitfalls

- UI text sized for a real phone is unreadable at rest in a 1080 frame: design the UI for the pushed-in shot (1.5×) and only show it at rest briefly.
- Floating cards stacked over the phone's status bar look like a glitch; stack them in the empty space above the phone, or over the lower half of the screen.
- Translucent cards let the phone show through and muddy the text: floating cards are opaque.
- CSS blur is slow: blur only the headline words while they enter, and the phone during its defocus. Draw the background blobs as radial gradients, never as blurred shapes.
- Everything inside the camera is redrawn on every frame it scales. Things that only drift (the blobs) or sit still behind a moving layer (the end card's ground) go on their own layer with `will-change: transform`, as do soft glows; never put it on the camera or on anything with text, which would be scaled blurry instead of redrawn.
- Don't let every move overshoot: overshoot is for badges and chips; the camera and the cards land with `circ.out` / `sine.out`.
- Copying a real app's interface, logo, wallpaper or layout makes it someone else's film: draw a generic UI in the brand's colours.
- White text on the contrast card or the accent tag disappears under a dark brand: use `--latar-2` on the contrast card and `--teks-di-aksen` on the accent.

## Measured from the references

- Films: 8 exemplars (cluster of 75)
- Median length: 44 s (cluster median 26 s)
- Cuts per minute: median 4.3 (cluster 3.8); 3 of 8 are a single continuous take
- Median shot length: 7.8 s
- Tempo where present: 83–143 BPM, typically ~120–128
- Camera moves: 175 measured; median move 0.37 s; median push-in 0.52 s
- Zoom factors: push-ins median 1.18× (interquartile 1.10–1.51×, deep dives up to 2.1–2.9×); pull-backs median 0.83× (lower quartile 0.77×)
- Most common fitted eases: `sine.out` (34), `circ.out` (30), linear (27), `power1.out` (13), `sine.in` (11), `power1.in` (10), `power2.inOut` (8), `power1.inOut` (8)

# Phone showcase: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 1.5, medium 2.4, long 3.6.

## hook

- en: two-line headline blurs in word by word over a phone rising from below; the camera pushes 1.12×
- id: judul dua baris muncul dari blur per kata di atas HP yang naik dari bawah; kamera mendorong 1,12×

## problem

- en: the camera dives 1.5× into the screen onto the pain (sold out, a long wait), asked above in one line
- id: kamera menyelam 1,5× ke layar pada masalahnya (stok habis, antre lama), ditanyakan satu baris di atas

## fact

- en: the phone recedes to ~0.55× and a bold two-line promise with pill chips takes the frame
- id: HP mundur mengecil ±0,55×, janji tebal dua baris dengan chip pil mengisi layar

## step

- en: a touch dot taps the screen, a ripple spreads and the screen moves to its next state
- id: titik sentuh mengetuk layar, riak menyebar, lalu layar pindah ke tahap berikutnya

## compare

- en: two cards lift out side by side over the defocused phone; the chosen one gets the main-colour ring
- id: dua kartu terangkat berdampingan di depan HP yang buram; yang dipilih diberi cincin warna utama

## number

- en: a contrast card slides up over the phone; the figure counts up in 1.1 s while small bars grow
- id: kartu kontras naik menutupi HP; angka dihitung naik 1,1 detik sementara batang kecil tumbuh

## proof

- en: notification cards drop in above the phone one by one, 0.16 s apart, each with a main-colour icon
- id: kartu notifikasi jatuh satu per satu di atas HP, selang 0,16 detik, ikonnya warna utama

## offer

- en: the camera dives and the screen scrolls, then the chosen card lifts out, bigger and tilted, phone defocused
- id: kamera menyelam dan layar bergulir, lalu kartu pilihan terangkat keluar, lebih besar dan miring, HP buram

## cta

- en: hard cut to the dark end card: logo tile, name, a pill with the contact, slow settle, held 2.4 s
- id: potong ke kartu penutup gelap: logo, nama, pil berisi kontak, mengendap pelan, diam 2,4 detik

## payoff

- en: the phone recedes small under the closing line, then a hard cut to the dark end card, held
- id: HP mundur mengecil di bawah kalimat penutup, lalu potong keras ke kartu penutup gelap, diam
